content.text:
LinkedIn wrapped the **Germany marketing page’s sample list**, not the public catalog. That is the same failure mode you already documented, and the live HTML still trains the wrapper to do it.

## What happened

LinkedIn’s wrapping crawler does not ingest Google sitemaps or `JobPosting` JSON-LD the way Google Jobs does. Unpaid wrapping crawls **one career-site-shaped HTML page** it already knows, extracts a short list of title / company / location / apply URL, and posts those as Basic Jobs. The XML feed at `/feeds/linkedin-jobs.xml` is not scraped until Talent BD accepts it.

`/relocation-jobs-germany` is that page. It has been in `sitemap.xml`, requested for indexing, and LinkedIn already wrapped strings from country pages once before — that is why `/jobs/<slug>` was built.

On the live Germany page right now, the only job-shaped block is **“Sample roles from company career pages”**: five Zalando titles, company + Berlin, and `href`s to **`jobs.zalando.com`**, not `kuchup.com/jobs/...`. The page has FAQ/Breadcrumb JSON-LD and **no `JobPosting`**. The only Kuchup job links on that page are the hub CTAs `/jobs` and `/jobs?country=germany`.

Those sample hrefs are baked at homepage build from the employer ATS URL:

```149:157:homepage/components/CountryCatalogPanel.tsx
            {state.sample_positions.map((role) => (
              <li key={`${role.company_name}-${role.title}-${role.url}`}>
                <a
                  href={role.url}
                  className="text-sm font-medium text-text-primary underline-offset-2 hover:underline"
                  target="_blank"
                  rel="noopener noreferrer"
                >
```

`role.url` comes from catalog `positions[].url` (Zalando’s board), not `public_slug`. The wrapper sees a tiny jobs list with real apply URLs and stops. Four public Zalando roles currently exist on both surfaces (`ZEOS`, Search and Browse, Lounge, Ad Platform). That is why you got **four** posts and they match the samples.

## Why `/jobs` was not wrapped

`/jobs` is doing what you built: 54 crawlable `/jobs/<slug>` pages, `JobPosting` in the first HTML response, `/sitemap-jobs.xml` with 54 URLs, LinkedIn XML with 54 `applyUrl`s on apex `kuchup.com/jobs/<slug>`. Germany hub alone has 40 of those.

LinkedIn still ignored that path because:

1. **It does not use your jobs sitemap.** Google might. Wrapping does not.
2. **The feed is inert until BD accepts it.** Hosting it does not start a 24h scrape.
3. **Wrapping recrawls the URL it already used.** That is the country page, not a 54-link hub one hop behind a new Flask route.
4. **The hub is an `ItemList` of links.** Wrapping wants job-detail pages or a careers RSS/XML. It will not reliably follow every slug.
5. **`/jobs` is new; the Germany page is not.** Docs for this funnel are from 7 Sep. Organic wrap lag is days to weeks, and it prefers the page it already posted from.
6. **Aggregator rules.** Bulk listings with `hiringOrganization: Kuchup` and a third-party employer in the title are exactly what LinkedIn’s job-board guidelines push back on. A handful of strings from a marketing page is easier to swallow than 54 aggregator detail pages.

So the SEO work helped Google’s crawl graph. It did not retarget LinkedIn’s wrapper. The wrapper is still eating the old bait.

## What I would change

If the goal is LinkedIn Apply → `https://kuchup.com/jobs/<slug>`:

- **Stop putting employer ATS URLs on country pages.** Point samples at `/jobs/{public_slug}`, or drop the sample job list. As long as Zalando links sit in static HTML on a page LinkedIn already wraps, that is what it will wrap.
- **Set the LinkedIn company Page website / wrapping source to `https://kuchup.com/jobs`**, not the homepage and not `/relocation-jobs-germany`.
- **Send BD the feed** with two or three real `/jobs/<slug>` URLs. That is the only documented bulk ingest. HTML wrapping will stay incomplete.
- **Clean titles** like `… Backend Berlin View job` in the scrape. Those strings are in both the samples and the catalog slugs; if LinkedIn posted them verbatim, that is extra proof it copied that list.

I would not expect sitemap resubmits or more `JobPosting` on `/jobs` to fix this. The leak is the Germany sample markup. If you want, I can switch those sample links to public slugs (or remove them) so the next wrap cannot use Zalando apply URLs.

content.text:
Yes. That is the cheapest experiment that can actually falsify the wrapping hypothesis: **same crawl target, different apply URL.** Leave sitemaps, the XML feed, and the LinkedIn company-page URL alone for now, or you will not know what caused the next wrap.

One constraint: **never fall back to the employer ATS.** If a sample has no `public_slug`, omit it. A mixed page (some `/jobs/…`, some `jobs.zalando.com`) would still feed LinkedIn the Zalando links.

How to read the result, when wrapping recrawls (days, not hours):

- **Worked:** a new Basic Job’s apply URL is `https://kuchup.com/jobs/<slug>`.
- **No recrawl:** the old four Zalando posts stay as they are. That is not a failed strategy.
- **Partial:** those four expire and nothing new appears. LinkedIn saw the list change and did not follow `/jobs/…`.

I wired that in. Country samples now link only to `/jobs/<slug>`, in the same tab, with no `target="_blank"`. The Germany static HTML no longer contains `jobs.zalando.com`. Live samples are the newest visa-positive roles (Sumup + FlixBus), not the four Zalando titles already wrapped — so this is “new list, Kuchup URLs,” not a same-title A/B on those four. If you want that tighter test, we can pin those Zalando slugs on the Germany page only.

This is in the local homepage export. LinkedIn will not see it until you deploy.
